messages:
sara-support: Heads up — P1 from Acme Payments (case #5821). On-prem HSM after last key rotation: signing latency spikes, intermittent 5xxs, and customer says audit events older than ~72h are missing. They want a compliance statement about key custody + proof of audit retention config. Details and logs below.

matt-crypto: Can you paste the raw HSM errors? Any PKCS#11 error codes? Also: which HSM vendor/firmware and hsm_agent version? We need to know if this is a firmware bug vs config.

sara-support: Paste from their hsm-agent logs (redacted customer data):
```
2026-11-02T14:12:03Z ERROR hsm_agent: sign request failed: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR
2026-11-02T14:12:03Z WARN  hsm_agent: session checkout latency=620ms pool_size=8
2026-11-02T14:12:04Z ERROR forwarder: audit write failed: "write timeout" to s3://acme-audits/2026-11-02.log
2026-11-05T09:04:11Z INFO  rotation: key rotation completed id=kp-xx-zz
2026-11-05T09:04:12Z ERROR hsm_agent: CKR_SESSION_COUNT
```
They also ran a quick load repro: 200 concurrent sign requests for 30s -> 7% 502/503 and median latency jumped from 350ms -> 2.1s. They say audit S3 bucket only contains files up to 3 days old despite SLA 90d.

jenna-ops: Is this Dedicated or Private? If Private/on-prem we don't control S3 retention; customer might have misconfigured lifecycle. Ask them for the audit-forwarder config and the S3 lifecycle policy. Also we should check hsm_agent metrics (session_count, checkout_latency, open_handles).

sara-support: It's Private (on-prem) with our hsm_agent and an internal forwarder that uploads to the customer's S3. They claim they didn't change lifecycle. I've asked for /etc/hsm/audit-forwarder.yaml and their bucket lifecycle.

thomas-enginfra: Two things to triage immediately: 1) if CKR_SESSION_COUNT is appearing, pool exhausted — we should try bumping pool_size as a mitigation; 2) the audit-forwarder write timeouts point to networking/S3 creds or throttling on their bucket. Ask them to run this and send output:
```bash
# check hsm_agent version and config
sudo systemctl status hsm_agent.service && sudo cat /etc/hsm/hsm_agent.conf
# forwarder config
sudo cat /etc/hsm/audit-forwarder.yaml
# quick pkcs11 smoke test
pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/libacme-pkcs11.so -T
```
If they can run those and paste results that helps.

matt-crypto: For the custody question: confirm we never export keys from the HSM. For on-prem we run the agent that talks to the local HSM — Redwood does not hold the private key. We can provide a signed attestation doc, but Security needs to OK the language. Elaine, can Security produce a custody attestation?

elaine-cs: Yes, we can draft an attestation stating: (a) keys are generated/managed in customer HSM (no export), (b) our agent only issues PKCS#11 calls, (c) we log HSM operations locally and optionally forward to customer S3. We need the HSM vendor & fw version and the agent version to include in the attestation. Also we need their consent to include their bucket path.

audit-bot: automated: export job started -> s3://redwood-audit-exports/acme-payments/2026-11-06-10-12.tar.gz (for internal review).

sara-support: Customer just sent the forwarder config snippet:
```yaml
forwarder:
  retention_days: 90
  batch_size: 50
  s3_bucket: acme-audits
  s3_region: us-west-2
  max_retries: 3
```
And their S3 lifecycle shows a rule that expires objects after 3 days (whoops). They insist they didn't touch it; could be an automated process.

jenna-ops: Ok that explains the missing events. For the signing errors: if lifecycle is independent issue, we still need to fix session exhaustion. Ask them to temporarily increase hsm_agent.pool_size to 32, restart the agent and run the same 200-concurrency repro to see if errors drop. Also gather `hsm_agent /metrics` (Prometheus) around the repro window.

matt-crypto: Also want to see HSM audit records (vendor side) for the rotation window. Some HSMs (vendor X) have known issues where rotation triggers ephemeral increase in session usage or rekey handshake that times out under concurrency. If vendor logs show device-side errors at rotation time, we'll escalate to vendor support.

thomas-enginfra: If they cannot bump pool_size (policy or resource limits), we can implement short-term fallback: route non-critical signing to a software key in our enclave (only for non-PII tokens) to smooth traffic during rotation windows. Need product/security approval.

elaine-cs: I'll draft attestation and include: agent version, hsm vendor/fw, that Redwood does not export keys, and the recommended mitigations. I need the exact hsm_agent log snippet and the forwarder config — Sara please attach sanitized logs in the ticket.

sara-support: Attached sanitized logs in the case and asked customer to run those commands and try pool_size bump. Next steps I'm proposing: 1) confirm S3 lifecycle (they found 3-day rule) -> customer will remove/adjust it; 2) customer to bump pool_size and run repro and share Prom metrics; 3) we get vendor audit logs and firmware info to see if rotation bug; 4) Security to sign attestation.

matt-crypto: Sounds good. If vendor audit logs show device errors at rotation time we open a vendor escalation and ask for fw rollback or patch. If it's config, we document recommended defaults (pool_size >= 32 for 200-concurrency, forwarder batch_size tuning, and S3 lifecycle >= SLA).

sara-support: I'll keep this thread updated. tagging: @matt-crypto @thomas-enginfra @elaine-cs @jenna-ops. Thanks. :pray:
